slides.title: What an HTTP request looks like
slides.html:
HTTP

What an HTTP request looks like

  • Method: what to do
  • URL: which resource
  • Headers: extra info like auth
  • Body: the data (POST, PATCH)

Request → Response

POST /api/tasks HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:5000
Content-Type: application/json
 
{ "title": "Read Express docs" }
 
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json
 
{ "id": 1, "title": "Read Express docs", "done": false }

slides.title: Your first Express server
slides.html:
Express

Your first Express server

  • express.json() reads JSON bodies
  • req: what came in
  • res: what you send back

server.js

import express from "express";
 
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
 
app.get("/api/health", (req, res) => {
  res.json({ ok: true, time: new Date() });
});
 
const PORT = process.env.PORT || 5000;
app.listen(PORT, () =>
  console.log(`API on http://localhost:${PORT}`));

slides.title: REST endpoints for tasks
slides.html:
REST

REST endpoints for tasks

  • Nouns in the URL, verbs in the method
  • Plural resource names
  • The same URL does different things per method

Task API

GET     /api/tasks          list tasks
GET     /api/tasks/:id      one task
POST    /api/tasks          create
PATCH   /api/tasks/:id      update some fields
DELETE  /api/tasks/:id      delete
 
GET     /api/tasks?done=true&q=read

slides.title: Params, query and body
slides.html:
Input

Params, query and body

  • req.params: /tasks/42
  • req.query: ?done=true
  • req.body: the JSON sent
  • Params and query are always strings

Reading input

app.get("/api/tasks/:id", (req, res) => {
  const id = Number(req.params.id);
  // ...
});
 
app.get("/api/tasks", (req, res) => {
  const { done, q } = req.query;  // strings or undefined
  // ...
});
 
app.post("/api/tasks", (req, res) => {
  const { title } = req.body;
});

slides.title: Middleware
slides.html:
Middleware

Middleware

  • Runs before your route handler
  • Can change req, respond, or call next()
  • Order matters: top to bottom

middleware.js

// logger
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  const start = Date.now();
  res.on("finish", () =>
    console.log(req.method, req.url, res.statusCode,
      `${Date.now() - start}ms`));
  next();
});
 
// validation for one route
const needTitle = (req, res, next) =>
  req.body.title ? next()
    : res.status(400).json({ message: "Title is required" });

slides.title: Routers and controllers
slides.html:
Structure

Routers and controllers

routes/tasks.js

import { Router } from "express";
import * as tasks from "../controllers/tasks.js";
 
const router = Router();
router.get("/", tasks.list);
router.get("/:id", tasks.getOne);
router.post("/", tasks.create);
router.patch("/:id", tasks.update);
router.delete("/:id", tasks.remove);
export default router;

server.js

import tasksRouter from "./routes/tasks.js";
 
app.use("/api/tasks", tasksRouter);

routes = which URL · controllers = what happens

slides.title: Error handling
slides.html:
Errors

Error handling

  • 404 middleware for unknown routes
  • Error middleware has 4 arguments
  • Express 5 catches async errors for you

server.js

// after all routes
app.use((req, res) => {
  res.status(404).json({ message: `Cannot ${req.method} ${req.url}` });
});
 
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  console.error(err);
  res.status(err.status || 500).json({
    message: err.status ? err.message : "Something went wrong",
  });
});

slides.title: The task controller
slides.html:
Build

The task controller

  • Validate before saving
  • Trim spaces from input
  • Return 201 with the new task

controllers/tasks.js

let tasks = [];
let nextId = 1;
 
export const create = (req, res) => {
  const title = req.body.title?.trim();
  if (!title) return res.status(400).json({ message: "Title is required" });
  const task = { id: nextId++, title, done: false, createdAt: new Date() };
  tasks.push(task);
  res.status(201).json(task);
};
